chunks: And from him, from al-Nadhr and Fadalah, from Abdullah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman who calls the adhan for the prayer, so he said: 'It is good; if she does it, and if she does not, it suffices her to say the takbir and to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever calls the adhan should pause at the end of each segment of his adhan, raise his voice, and not lower his breath so much that he cannot hear himself, until the end of the chapter.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq), peace be upon him
key_terms.أَجْزَأَهَا: It suffices her / is valid for her
key_terms.الشَّيْخُ: The Sheikh (referring to the author/compiler, likely al-Tusi)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a woman to call the adhan in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility of women performing the adhan, a point of scholarly discussion regarding gender roles in public worship rituals. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the core obligation is limited to the takbir and the two shahadas, while Shaykh al-Tusi adds procedural nuances regarding vocal projection and pausing. This reflects the Shia juristic view that the adhan is a recommended act (mustahabb) rather than a strict pillar, allowing for flexibility in its performance by both men and women.
